title: Horizontal distance across quadrants
observableEvidence: Finds the horizontal distance between points that share a y-coordinate using the absolute value of their x-coordinate difference.
prompt: Points A(-6, 4) and B(3, 4) are on a coordinate plane. How far apart are they?
solutionRepresentation: The points share y-coordinate 4, so the horizontal distance is |3 - (-6)| = 9 units.
solutionMethod: Subtract the x-coordinates and use absolute value for distance.

deterministicValidator.equivalenceNotes: Accept 9 with or without the unit.

hintSteps.prompt: The matching y-coordinates mean the segment is horizontal.
hintSteps.question: Which coordinates should be compared for a horizontal distance?

review.originalityStatement: New candidate item drafted for this repository; it does not reproduce or paraphrase proprietary or contest material.

accessibilityNotes: Present the ordered pairs and question as plain text; no coordinate-plane image is required.
accessibleAlternative: Read aloud or display: Point A has x negative 6 and y 4. Point B has x 3 and y 4. They are on the same horizontal line. State the distance in units.
